title: Activation-Free Backbones for Image Recognition: Polynomial Alternatives within MetaFormer-Style Vision Models
claim: Our method gives higher accuracy than both standard baselines and prior specialized approaches at every model scale and compute budget.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots sharing y-axis, legend inside right panel
description: Two side-by-side line plots share a y-axis of ImageNet top-1 accuracy, which runs from about 77 to 85. The left panel plots accuracy against model size in millions of parameters. The right panel plots accuracy against FLOPs in G. Each panel has six curves. The two proposed models are drawn as bold solid lines in blue with squares and orange with circles, and they sit at the top of both panels. Two MetaFormer baselines, ConvFormer and CAFormer, are faint dotted green and pink lines just below them. Two prior polynomial networks, MONet in purple and DTTN in brown, are dotted lines far below. The eye goes first to the solid orange and blue curves at the top. A legend in the lower right of the right panel labels all six models.
caption: ImageNet-1K accuracy comparison. Our polynomial backbones (CPolyNeXt, APolyNeXt) consistently outperform MetaFormer instantiations (ConvFormer, CAFormer) and prior polynomial networks (MONet, DTTN) across model scales. Curves show accuracy vs.\ (a) parameters and (b) FLOPs.
abstract: Modern vision backbones treat pointwise activations (e.g., ReLU, GELU) and exponential softmax as essential sources of nonlinearity, but we demonstrate they are not required within MetaFormer-style vision backbones. We design activation-free polynomial alternatives for three core primitives (MLPs, convolutions, and attention), where Hadamard products replace standard nonlinearities to yield polynomial functions of the input. These modules integrate seamlessly into existing architectures: instantiated within MetaFormer, a modular framework for vision backbones, our PolyNeXt models match or exceed activation-based counterparts across model scales on ImageNet classification, ADE20K semantic segmentation, and out-of-distribution robustness. We also substantially outperform prior polynomial networks at reduced computational cost, showing that polynomial variants of standard modules beat complex custom architectures.
